text:
maria: Quick thread — we hit an observability gap last night when a noisy tenant caused our sampling budget to spike. want to propose a small UX + policy change for route-level sensitivity so ops can throttle only high-risk routes.

sam: Context? which tenant / route? any PII leakage incidents?

maria: No confirmed leak, logs show large request bodies with email-like tokens, our sampler just sampled uniformly and burned through inspect budget.

anya: Oof. So current behavior is global sampler -> per-tenant quota -> fallback to drop? we don't have per-route weight adjustments, right?

kevin: Correct. Current chain: global rate-limit -> sticky sampler keyed by tenant -> when budget exhausted we stop capturing request bodies but keep metadata. No route sensitivity.

maria: Proposal sketch: add per-route sensitivity score (LOW/MED/HIGH) + console toggle to cap inspect TTL and sample rate per sensitivity. Default MED for user-content routes, HIGH for routes with attachments/credit-card-like heuristics.

sam: How do we compute sensitivity? heuristics (regex/email/cc), model detector, or manual route annotations?

anya: Hybrid. Autodetect heuristics + allow product teams to annotate routes via API. Console shows recommended sensitivity with reason.

kevin: Need to consider cost/complexity: adding another dimension to sampling decision tree will affect the sampler hot path. We should precompute sensitivity in the router and attach a small enum to request context so sampler logic stays O(1).

maria: Exactly. Router annotates request with sensitivity and a short provenance tag: e.g., `sensitivity=HIGH:heuristic=email-cc` or `sensitivity=LOW:annotated`. Sampler checks that string.

sam: UX: console control should expose three knobs per route: base-sample-rate, inspect-ttl, and override policy (enforced / recommend). If product sets enforced, ops can still breakglass.

kevin: Breakglass needs audit trail. ops-bot should emit an event when breakglass toggled with who/why. Add retention <-> legal.

ops-bot: deploy event: sampling-breakglass-v1 enabled in canary.

anya: Edge-case: what about fallback routing? If a region falls back to cheaper model variant, we must ensure sampling heuristics remain the same. Otherwise we lose provenance. Router should propagate sensitivity across fallbacks.

maria: Agree. Also want a backstop: if sensitivity detector yields HIGH but tenant has opted out of inspect, we should still record decision but not persist payload. i.e., record metadata + hashed fingerprint.

sam: Fingerprint hashing: we need deterministic but salted per-tenant to avoid cross-tenant correlation. Recommend HMAC with tenant key + truncated hex.

kevin: Perf note: HMAC per request is ok but avoid expensive KMS calls. Use cached per-tenant ephemeral keys rotated daily.

anya: Security ask: store sensitivity provenance in a single header in logs to make downstream scrubbing deterministic. e.g., `x-rd-sensitivity: HIGH;detector=email-v1`

maria: Example config for console UI (rough):
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "sensitivity": "HIGH",
  "base_sample_rate": 0.02,
  "inspect_ttl_seconds": 86400,
  "override": "recommend"
}
```

sam: Nice. Can we also show simulated budget impact over time when people change rates? big ask for product but helps adoption.

kevin: We can estimate token-level cost using existing telemetry: take recent per-route token histogram * new sample_rate -> delta tokens/day. Should be straightforward as a backend job.

maria: Rollout plan: 1) add router annotation + header, 2) sampler reads header and applies simple lookup, 3) console UI behind feature flag with simulation, 4) canary enforce on 10% of routes.

anya: For the canary we should enable detailed metrics: sampled_count_by_sensitivity, budget_burn_by_route, inspect_hits_blocked_by_optout.

sam: One more: ensure audit logs do not include raw payload when sensitivity=HIGH unless inspect allowed. Many audits only look at 'decision' fields.

kevin: Implementation note: keep sampler code path minimal. No regex scanning in sampler. Router does heavy work asynchronously or via fast deterministic checks.

maria: I'll draft a short RFC and a console mock. tagging @kevin @anya to review. thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: sampler-router-annotate v0.3 -> canary cluster at 2026-03-20T03:22:30Z

maria: filing RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfc/route-sensitivity-sampling (WIP)

kevin: i'll review the RFC this afternoon.

anya: happy to pair on console sim next week.

sam: thx — let's keep the canary tight and monitor `inspect_budget_pct` metric.
